note: Round-2 owner answers on Group A. Owner also directed a careful re-read of the slip footers/notes; slips 18, 49 and 97 were re-opened at full size and re-verified. Findings recorded below.

decisions.memo: เมนไปทำใบขับขี่
decisions.note: Driving licence for Ming treated as an operating cost rather than a staff advance/receivable. Branch still not stated.

decisions.reread_finding: Re-opened at full size. The complete Bangkok Bank slip card is visible from header through เลขที่อ้างอิง and QR, and there is NO memo/note row rendered at all — unlike other Bangkok Bank slips in this batch, which do show one. The absence is confirmed, not a crop artefact.
decisions.additional_observation: The recipient line reads 'MR. AUNG MIN PHAY SON - / เติมเงินพร้อมเพย์ / G-Wallet / K Plus Wallet, e-wallet 00499-915-311-5661'. This is a WALLET TOP-UP, not a standard account transfer. A top-up moves funds into a wallet; it does not itself evidence what the funds were later spent on.
decisions.caveat: Booked to OPEX on owner instruction. The business purpose remains unevidenced by any document in this batch. This is an owner-approved classification, not an observation (OCR_RULES 7 — approval never turns an unknown into an observation).

decisions.memo: ข้าวเหนียวมูน 5 กิโล
decisions.why: Slip 19 is a ฿900 sticky-rice purchase from นาง เพ็ญวิไล สถานทรัพย์ on 30/08/2026 — an ingredient, not a capital item. Booking it as CAPEX would be plainly wrong and has NOT been applied.
decisions.likely_intent: Probable slip-number typo. The nearest CAPEX candidate in the list presented to the owner is slip 41, 'Durian shop invest : acylic box 1 pcs', ฿1,500. Not assumed — awaiting the owner's corrected slip number.

decisions.memo: ค่าแรงพนักงานเดือนสิงหาคม
decisions.owner_answer: no it's not [a different person] — i use own acc to withdraw cash
decisions.interpretation: The transfer moves funds between the owner's own accounts so cash can be withdrawn and paid to staff. The bank transfer is the funding mechanism; the economic event is an August staff wage cost of ฿11,500, which is a genuine OPEX expense.
decisions.caveat: DOUBLE-BOOKING WATCH: because the slip funds a cash payment rather than paying a payee directly, this ฿11,500 must not be booked alongside any separate evidence of the same cash wages. Must be reconciled against slips 26, 27, 101, 111 and 72 and against existing Daily_Expenses rows before import.
decisions.consistent_with: CLAUDE.md — cash payments to staff frequently have no bank trace; absence of a direct payee record is not evidence of non-payment.

decisions.memo_verbatim: สับปะรด 55 กิโล (35 ลูก) โลละ 50 บาท รวม 1925
decisions.reread_finding: Footer re-verified character by character at full size; the memo is transcribed correctly as recorded.

check_update.explanation: The written unit price 'โลละ 50 บาท' is an error in the note. The quantity (35 ลูก / 55 กิโล) and the total (฿1,925) are correct and agree with the amount paid. The ฿825 discrepancy was caused by the mis-written unit price, not by a wrong quantity or a wrong payment.
check_update.note: The erroneous raw text is preserved; it was not overwritten.

decisions.memo: ข้าวเหนียวมูน 2 โล + กะทิ
decisions.note: Full ฿360 booked to Sticky Rice; the กะทิ (coconut milk) is part of the sticky-rice preparation and is not split out as a separate coconut cost.

decisions.owner_answer: ฝา = lids or caps, ทิชชู่ = tissue, book as cogs
decisions.note: Both components booked to COGS per owner instruction; tissue treated as consumable packaging rather than a shop supply.

memo_verbatim: น้ำ 50ลิตร ลิตรละ45บาท
เนื้อคว้าน 50kg.กิโลละ 100บาท
annotation_verbatim: น้ำมะพร้าว และเนื้อมะพร้าว
decisions.owner_answer: 8100 = น้ำมะพร้าว 50 ลิตร ลิตรละ 45 บาท / เนื้อมะพร้าว 50 กิโล กิโลละ 100 บาท / ค่าส่ง 350 บาท
decisions.reread_finding: Footer re-opened at full size and verified character by character. The note does read 50 ลิตร and 50 kg exactly as transcribed. The owner's restatement matches the note — but the note's own figures do not reach the amount paid.
decisions.why_still_blocked: Restating the note does not close the ฿500 gap, because the gap is between the note and the bank, not a transcription error. Two candidate explanations remain and they produce different books: (a) a quantity on the day exceeded what was written — 55 kg of meat would give exactly 8,100 — making the whole ฿8,100 coconut COGS; (b) the ฿500 overpayment the owner raised earlier, leaving ฿7,600 as COGS and ฿500 as a supplier advance. A reading has NOT been selected on the grounds that it balances (OCR_RULES 3).
questions_for_owner: Was the actual delivery larger than the note states (e.g. 55 kg of coconut meat rather than 50)?
Or was ฿500 an overpayment — and if so, was it credited against a later delivery?

decisions.note: Both components booked to OPEX per owner instruction, including the ฿1,721 'other equipment' which is therefore expensed rather than capitalised.
Porterage booked to OPEX rather than COGS/Transportation.

summary.branch_allocation_still_open: Most resolved slips still carry no stated branch. Shared-pool COGS is allocated downstream by rule, but the OPEX/Salary rows (8, 18, 25, 102, 105) need a branch before import.
